transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-16 14:00 PDT | Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Harper Diaz (Redwood CSM) - Jasmine Ortiz (Cascade Head of Eng), Mark Rivera (CTO), Priya Singh (Head of Data), Evan Lowe (PM)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick agenda: results from last week's tuning, latency/throughput benchmarks, quality numbers on the sample intents, security follow-ups, and then next steps for closing the business case. sound right?

[00:18] Jasmine: yep sounds good, thanks Maya.

[00:22] Liam: hi all, i will walk through the benchmarks first - caveat that these runs were on our dedicated pool with the quantized 8-bit variant we discussed, so numbers will differ slightly in hosted.

[00:35] [louder crosstalk] Mark: ok perfect, show us the p50/p95, and also any tail latency spikes you saw.

[00:42] Liam: cool. so summary first: median latency (p50) across the 5k sample was about 85ms in steady state for single-turn generation with 256 token context, p95 around 210ms, p99 around 480ms. throughput with batching tuned to 64 was ~220 req/s sustained. these are with KV-cache warm for common prefixes; cold-starts added ~120ms on average.

[01:10] Priya: just to clarify, those numbers are on dedicated GPUs in our staging region?

[01:14] Liam: yes staging dedicated pool in us-west, config matches the POC cluster we provisioned for you. memory and kernel selection were optimized; we tried FP16 and int8 quantization paths. int8 gave ~1.8x cost reduction with a small delta in some quality metrics.

[01:34] Jasmine: small delta meaning how much? we need to keep intent accuracy above 90% for our key flows.

[01:39] Liam: on the 1.2k labeled validation subset you shared earlier, int8 quantization dropped intent match rates from 94.1% to 92.6% on the top-5 intent mapping; for slot extraction F1 it was 0.02 absolute drop. so still within acceptable range for most flows but the purchase-path microflow saw a 3% drop in precise sku extraction in a small number of long-context prompts.

[02:06] Evan: that's actually pretty good. where did errors cluster? long receipts or multi-turn clarifications?

[02:12] Liam: mostly long receipt-like inputs and cases where the prompt included OCR artifacts. we also saw a couple where prefix caching evicted kv entries because of aggressive batching and sequence length variation.

[02:25] Maya: ok noted. we can tweak cache retention and batching policies per-route - Redwood has per-route batching and cache TTL that you can set. for the purchase microflow we typically recommend a smaller batch size and pinning the route to a low-latency instance group.

[02:44] Mark: cost estimate—how does this look at scale? we ran a back-of-envelope for our holiday peak at 1.2M tokens/day.

[02:50] Liam: on the quantized int8 profile you're looking at roughly $2,300 a month for the token compute for those volumes on Dedicated pricing in the pilot config; hosted numbers are slightly higher but give you auto-failover. with caching we also see effective token reductions of ~18% on prefix heavy queries, so unit cost comes down.

[03:10] Priya: can you send the exact assumptions? e.g., sequence length avg, tokens per call, and the math.

[03:14] Maya: yes i'll send the pricing sheet and the assumptions. action: maya will follow up with updated pricing and commitment tiers.

[03:22] [00:03:24] Jasmine: switching to quality - priya has the eval set results?

[03:28] Priya: yes i took the 5k annotated prompts, split into dev/validation, ran the Redwood output through our intent classifier. overall top-1 match at baseline (no quant) was 94.1%, with int8 at 92.6 like Liam said. for our top 12 intents - the purchase, returns, and price-checks - we're above 90; the long-receipt SKU extraction was 87 without heuristic postprocessing.

[03:55] Evan: do you see any regressions that would impact core KPI in week-1 metrics? we need less than 2% failure on checkout flows.

[04:02] Priya: with a small postprocess where we canonicalize skus and run a secondary regex fallback, failures drop to 0.8%. so it's a mitigatable gap.

[04:12] Maya: good to hear. one thing we recommend is shipping with a light postprocess fallback for recognized high-risk flows while we continue to iterate model/prune prompts.

[04:20] [laugh] Mark: pragmatic. procurement will love the fallback.

[04:26] Harper: quick security check-in - you asked for SOC2 and SAML details. we uploaded the SOC2 summary to the shared drive and the SAML SSO integration guide; i'll drop the link in chat after.

[04:37] Jasmine: for data residency, we need EU region support for some flows. do you support region pinning on private/dedicated?

[04:45] Maya: yes we support region pinning on Dedicated and Private. for Hosted API we have region options but for full EU-only residency you should use Dedicated or Private with our VPC option.

[04:56] Priya: also KMS integration - will Redwood integrate with our HSM and KMS for key management?

[05:02] Liam: yes we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated; for hosted there's a bring-your-own-key pathway but with different rotation controls. we'll share the KMS integration doc.

[05:14] Mark: timeline for compliance docs? we have an internal audit next month.

[05:18] Harper: i'll email the SOC2 attestation and privacy addendum today and can set up a call with our security team next week if helpful.

[05:26] Jasmine: perfect. next: success criteria to close the pilot and move to dedicated commit. we had listed earlier: 1) p50 latency <200ms for purchase path, 2) quality top-1 intent >=90% on key flows, 3) throughput >=200 req/s sustained, 4) procurement signoff / budget. are we aligned?

[05:44] Maya: that matches what we have. i'd add stability (no more than 1% error rate over 24h) as an operational metric.

[05:51] Priya: agreed. let's make the thresholds explicit in the SOW so there's no ambiguity.

[05:57] Liam: operational notes: we recommend a canary rollout for production with 10% traffic for 24-48h before full cutover, and automatic fallback to a smaller model variant for extreme tail events. that keeps cost predictable and maintains availability.

[06:13] Mark: about fallback - what's the delta in quality when falling back?

[06:17] Liam: fallback to the 6B variant increases latency slightly but cuts compute cost ~40%; quality drop on top-1 intent is typically 2-4% depending on the flow, so you get a graceful degradation not a hard failure.

[06:31] Jasmine: ok good. procurement question: if we sign a 12-month dedicated commit do we get a better price and reserved capacity guarantees?

[06:39] Maya: yes, dedicated commits give you both price discounts and a guaranteed capacity pool with SLA. i'll include the tiered discounts in the pricing doc — examples for 6/12/24 month terms.

[06:50] Evan: one technical ask - can we run an end-to-end benchmark with our real prod sample (5k prompts) including OCR noise and multi-turn chains? we want to replicate user patterns not perfectly sanitized dev data.

[06:59] Liam: absolutely, that's what we planned. please send the sample set, and we will run it on the POC cluster and share the raw logs and per-prompt latency distributions.

[07:10] Priya: i'll package and upload the annotated set by tomorrow. also can you include tokenization stats and token-level cost per prompt?

[07:16] Liam: yes will include tokenization and token cost breakdown and per-route cost.

[07:22] [07:22] Mark: circle back on the data retention question - how long are logs retained in the POC and can we toggle retention?

[07:29] Harper: default retention for pilot is 90 days in the console, but we can change retention per account and we have an API to purge logs. also audit logs are kept per contract terms.

[07:38] Jasmine: great, please add that to the security doc.

[07:42] Maya: quick note on the benchmark results we showed: p95 at 210ms was driven by some cold-kv cases and a small percent of long-sequence jobs. with the recommended per-route batching and cache tweaks we expect p95 to drop to ~160-170ms. we'll validate in the 5k run.

[07:58] Evan: do you have an example of a per-route config? we'd like to see memory and batch settings.

[08:03] Liam: yes i'll attach sample config yml - note: the config uses batch_target=32 for high-throughput routes and batch_target=8 for low latency ones, plus cache_ttl settings.

[08:13] Priya: are there any constraints for our on-prem evaluation? we may want to test Private in a later phase.

[08:19] Maya: Private requires on-prem infra and an install cycle, usually 6-8 weeks including validation and network setup; Dedicated is faster to stand up. if data residency and strict control are must-haves, Private is the final target.

[08:33] Mark: budget and timeline - if the pilot shows we meet success criteria, procurement target is sign in next sprint, so 2-3 weeks.

[08:41] Maya: great. so immediate next steps we'll run the 5k real-sample benchmark, tweak cache/batching for purchase path, share updated pricing and SOW with explicit success criteria, and security doc circulation.

[08:54] Jasmine: can we get an explicit date for the benchmark results?

[08:58] Liam: we'll run the job within 24 hours of receiving the sample; aim to deliver results by 2026-06-19 EOD.

[09:06] Priya: i'll upload the prompt set today.

[09:10] Harper: i'll send the SOC2/ISO summary and the SAML/KMS docs after the call.

[09:15] Maya: awesome. any final questions or blockers?

[09:19] Mark: not from engineering. procurement will need the official pricing sheet and SOW to push forward.

[09:24] Maya: understood, i'll get that sent by Thursday. Harper will push the security docs today. Liam will run the benchmark and share logs on Friday. Priya will provide the sample today. Mark will confirm procurement timeline by next Tuesday.

[09:36] Jasmine: thanks, really appreciate the focus on measurable success criteria.

[09:39] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in writing and update the CRM.

[09:44] [end call]

Notes / summary:
- Benchmarks show p50 ~85ms, p95 ~210ms with recommended per-route tuning expected to lower p95 to ~160ms. throughput ~220 req/s with batching=64. cold-starts add ~120ms.
- Int8 quantization reduces compute cost (~1.8x) with small quality drop; top-1 intent falls from 94.1% -> 92.6% in validation set.
- Purchase microflow had SKU extraction gap (~87%); mitigated with a postprocess regex canonicalization bringing failure below 1%.
- Security: SOC2 summary, SAML SSO guide, KMS/HSM integration supported; Harper to share docs. EU data residency supported on Dedicated/Private.
- Success criteria for pilot close: p50 <200ms for purchase path, top-1 intent >=90% on key flows, throughput >=200 req/s, procurement signoff/budget.
- Next steps: pricing & SOW (Maya), 5k E2E benchmark (Liam), annotated dataset upload (Priya), security docs (Harper), procurement timeline confirmation (Mark).

References and links mentioned: pricing sheet (will be shared), SOC2 summary (shared to drive), SAML/KMS integration guide (Harper to link).

End transcript.
